scores.notes: Adam lies dead on a mat with mourners around him; no lettering, frame, bare edge or malformed figures.
Fire and sulfur rain from a dark sky onto the two cities with small figures on the path below; paint runs to all four edges and nothing is lettered.

Holmes's face clearly reads as Benedict Cumberbatch, with the dark curls and long dark coat of the screen version (centre). The slip in his hand and the letters on the table carry rows of unreadable printed lines.
Jesus sleeps on a cushion in the stern while disciples wake him in the storm; no faults seen.

The same bearded prophet is painted twice in the foreground, and the right seraph carries tongs and a coal from a later verse (only the centre seraph has six wings). A white robe is draped over the throne seat and arms in the shape of a seated lap with its train down the steps, though no head or torso is shown.
Father directs servants bringing the robe, sandals and ring to the returned son; no faults seen.
A filled treasury of gold and vessels with no figure of Wisdom drawn; no lettering or frame.
Hare and Hatter lean on the sleeping Dormouse at the table corner with Alice in an armchair at the end; the hat tag is blank. White paper shows at the edges, strongest on the right (accepted).
Moses points the way while the people pack up below the cloud-covered mountain; God appears only as cloud and light. White paper shows around the edges (accepted).
Job stands before the whirlwind, which holds no face or body; no faults seen.

Holmes (second from left) reads as Peter Cushing, the screen Holmes. The station-master's paper and the small wall plaque carry dotted unreadable lines; the smoke column, train and station otherwise match the text.
Fire rains on two burning cities with small fleeing figures; painted to the edges, no signature or lettering.
The king presses his signet into clay while men drag the stone over the den mouth and lords look on; no lettering or signature in the corners.
Four winged creatures covered in eyes stand on a glassy floor around a throne that holds only coloured mist and a veil, no body; the seer in the foreground and crowned elders belong to the vision.
Alice at the tea table with the Dormouse, March Hare and Hatter with tea and bread-and-butter; the pale-faced Hatter is not a clear likeness of any film actor and nothing is lettered.

Glowing glyph-like script covers the plaster wall at right beside two hands of light; it is invented pseudo-script, not legible writing. Daniel before the seated king is otherwise as the text describes.

The paper label lying on the glass table and the tag on its string both carry squiggle writing that cannot be read. Alice drinking from the bottle in the hall matches the text; paint reaches the edges.
Daniel is hauled out of the stone pit on ropes while the king leans over the rim; white paper shows along the top and sides (accepted).

Watson crouches with his revolver on a crate while Holmes stands by the lantern and Jones and Merryweather wait; no lettering. Holmes's gaunt profile at left resembles Peter Cushing but is too stylised to call a clear likeness. Ragged white paper shows at the top-left edge (accepted).
Waves break into the boat as the disciples bail and haul on the sail, with Jesus asleep in the stern and other boats nearby; no faults seen.
Egyptian chariots and horsemen charge along the seabed between two walls of water; chariot ornament is geometric, not lettering, and paint reaches the edges.
The Egyptian chariots charge toward the viewer in the foreground while the Israelite crowd and Moses stand behind them facing the same way, so the pursuers are ahead of the people they chase.
Moses sits on a stone with Aaron and Hur each holding up a hand at sunset above the battle; painted to the edges, hem ornament is not lettering.
An elder sets a stone in the wall among workers with Jerusalem and the temple behind; no faults seen.
The camp stays pitched around the tabernacle under a formless pillar of cloud; no faults seen.
David with his sling faces Goliath as he pitches forward with a small dark wound on his brow, both armies watching; the wound is not gory and nothing is lettered.
Daniel stands unharmed among resting lions beside a glowing winged angel while the king looks down from the opening; paint reaches the edges.

Four winged creatures covered in eyes (lion, calf, man, eagle) stand on a glassy floor; the centre is fire and cloud over a gold chest with carrying poles rather than a throne, with no figure in it. Pale walls are painted, not bare paper.
The father runs with open arms toward his ragged son on the road outside the town, the instant before the embrace; hands and limbs are sound.
Peter grips the lame man's hand and lifts him at the temple gate with John beside him and a crowd watching; the grip is on the man's left hand, a small slip that does not change the scene.

Holmes at left reads as Peter Cushing, with magnifying glass and bent pipe. The station-master's paper carries ruled unreadable lines. The burning whitewashed house and three fire engines are shown, but the party walks away from the fire and the engineer is drawn as a small boy.

Holmes, facing front at centre while he shutters the lantern, clearly reads as Peter Cushing. The vault, crates, Watson's revolver, Jones and Merryweather fit the text. Ragged white paper shows at the lower corners (accepted).
The father embraces his ragged son on the road with the house in the distance; white paper shows on all sides (accepted).

Alice with the flamingo, the Cat above and the smiling Queen close behind match the text, but the three courtiers at far right are ordinary full-bodied people in Tudor dress (one with red pips on his doublet), not flat cards. White paper shows around the edges (accepted).
A cloaked ruler sets a block into the wall beside workers with the city and temple behind; white paper shows along the top and sides (accepted).
Moses raises his rod at the rock as water pours out and the people and their animals drink; no faults seen.
Saul hurls the spear as David, harp in hand, twists away and the point strikes the wall; no spirit figure is drawn.
The Israelites walk the dry seabed between two walls of water at night, led by a man with a staff; no figure of God.

The tag on the Hatter's hat carries an unreadable glyph and scribbled papers lie on the floor. The Hatter with bitten teacup and bread, Hare arm-in-arm with the Dormouse, King, spectacled Queen and jury with slates match the text; a second crowned card-king stands at lower right.

A loose page in the satchel at lower right shows Latin letters that read like 'The cone of Dodiq...', and the open scroll is covered in rows of script. The whole picture is an aged scribe writing the book, a narrator figure the verse does not name, with an old couple seated behind.
Formless light breaks through mist over a dark sea under black cloud; no figure, lettering or frame.
